I used Claude Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Astra to build a self-learning trading algorithm

The result: +$2,786.41 in 9 days

1,508 launches tracked. 30,160 holders analyzed. 69 wallet clusters detected. Only 6 tokens passed every check, each scoring 85+/100

I MADE THE CORE SCORING CODE OPEN SOURCE (80+ STARS)

GitHub:https://t.co/vaBkwbtFMN

QUANTUMORB IS FULLY OPERATIONAL

- The website, RADAR, SCANNER, Tg bot and entire backend infrastructure are now live
- Hundreds of users are already using QuantumOrb daily

Three recent Solana launches:

Oct 30, 18:08 UTC: $WASTED launched → RADAR alert at 18:49 → 5.1x after the alert

Nov 2, 11:34 UTC: $MAMESUKE launched → RADAR alert at 12:16 → 7.6x after the alert

Nov 3, 21:21 UTC: $AMD launched → RADAR alert at 22:39 → 9.4x after the alert

Here’s how QuantumOrb works:

RADAR tracks new https://t.co/DVKX2i8Gnz launches, bonding curves, market caps and trading activity in real time

SHIELD checks creators before alerts go out. 10+ launches with fewer than 10% graduating? Flagged

SCANNER analyzes the top 20 holders and first 20 buyers, tracking wallet histories, entries and token distribution

CARTOGRAPHER detects connected wallets through shared token sources, same-transaction buys and transfers

GUARD investigates developer history, launch-slot accumulation and remaining dev holdings

ORB combines five risk signals into a 0–100 score and calculates potential selling impact using two models:

Risk Scoring Model

Score = S_operator + S_fresh + S_transfers + S_snipers + S_top20

The system evaluates hidden ownership, fresh wallets, transferred supply, early snipers and holder concentration

Price Impact Model

Impact = 1 − (R / (R + q))²

R = token reserves in the liquidity pool
q = tokens sold by connected wallets

The model estimates how much the price could fall if a linked group exits its positions

RADAR identifies potential runners. SCANNER reveals who’s actually behind them

One system. Real-time alerts. On-chain risk analysis.

QUANTUMORB IS LIVE

And we’re just getting started

items.title: THIS MIGHT BE ONE OF THE MOST INSANE AI PROJECTS ON GITHUB RIGHT NOW.
items.summary:
THIS MIGHT BE ONE OF THE MOST INSANE AI PROJECTS ON GITHUB RIGHT NOW.

121,000 stars. An entire AI-powered trading firm, open-sourced for anyone to explore.

And the crazy part? Every role is handled by an AI agent.

Analysts. Researchers. Traders. Risk managers. Portfolio managers.

Here's what's inside:

«4 analyst agents covering fundamentals, sentiment, news, and technicals.

Bull and bear agents that debate every potential trade before a decision is made.

A trader agent that determines when to enter and how much to allocate.

A 3-agent risk team with aggressive, neutral, and conservative strategies.

A portfolio manager that reviews, approves, or rejects every order.

Support for Claude, GPT, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek, and local models.

Built-in backtesting to evaluate strategies against historical data.»

Want to turn it into your own AI trading system? Here's the workflow:

1. Clone the repository and open it in Claude Code.

2. Ask Opus 5.5 to explain every agent in plain English so you understand how decisions are made.

3. Choose your models and configure your API keys. Use stronger models for critical decisions and cheaper ones for less demanding tasks.

4. Start with one ticker you understand. Read the full bull-versus-bear debate before trusting any output.

5. Run the built-in backtest over the last 3 years, including realistic fees and slippage. If it can't outperform buy-and-hold after costs, investigate before going further.

6. Explore broker integration, such as Alpaca for stocks or Binance for crypto.

7. Add strict safeguards: fixed position sizing, stop-loss rules, daily loss limits, and an emergency kill switch.

8. Run it in paper-trading mode for at least two weeks. Compare its performance with the backtest.

9. Connect Telegram for decision alerts. Only consider live trading after thorough testing, starting with an amount you can afford to lose.

One important reminder: an impressive AI trading architecture doesn't guarantee profitable trades. Test every strategy and never hand over your capital blindly.

Save this. You'll want to explore it.

items.title: MARC ANDREESSEN WENT ON ROGAN FOR OVER 3 HOURS. HERE ARE THE 17 THINGS WORTH YOUR ATTENTION.
items.summary:
MARC ANDREESSEN WENT ON ROGAN FOR OVER 3 HOURS. HERE ARE THE 17 THINGS WORTH YOUR ATTENTION.

1. AGI is already here, in his view. He says the line got crossed about 3 months ago with GPT-5.5, Claude 4.6, Gemini 3, and Grok 4.3, and nobody noticed because the field moves too fast to register milestones anymore.

2. For almost any topic, he says the top models now give him better answers than the world-class experts he could call by phone, and he can call almost anyone. Worth noting he has not published data behind this, and a separate Nature Medicine study on a comparable AI health tool found it missed real emergencies more than half the time. Take the claim seriously, verify it yourself.

3. His claim on doctors: they are already using ChatGPT in the exam room, typing your symptoms in the moment you stop talking. His actual quote: "at that point you're asking the question of like, what do I need you for."

4. Reportedly, when AI declines to answer something, he tells it he's writing a novel to get past the refusal.

5. Reportedly, his technique for hard topics is escalating simplicity: explain it like I'm 10, then 5, then 2, until it clicks.

6. Reportedly, instead of asking for the "right" answer, he has the AI steelman both sides of a hard question, then decides himself.

7. Reportedly, for big questions he has the AI role-play a panel of experts arguing with each other.

8. His broader point: the moment you think "I don't know how to figure this out" is exactly when most people give up, and exactly when you should open the AI instead.

9. His view: the only real skill left is knowing what to ask. The bottleneck is in your head, not the model.

10. He describes sending AI photos, rashes, blood tests, for a fast second opinion, since current models read images directly.

11. He points to CBT as the one clinically proven therapy type that AI can plausibly deliver on its own, meaning real therapeutic support becomes freely available at scale.

12. He cites AI cracking previously unsolved math problems, with early signs of the same happening in physics, chemistry, and biology.

13. Reportedly, he claims the top AI coders in Silicon Valley now earn as much as $50 million a year, which he uses as a signal of how large this shift actually is.

14. Reportedly, a friend paid to sequence his own DNA, fed it to an AI along with blood work and wearable data, and got back a working health dashboard.

15. Reportedly, another friend set up cameras in his home jiu-jitsu gym so AI could review his sparring and give him technique notes.

16. He coined the term "AI vampire" for the pattern of people working more and sleeping less because AI keeps making more output possible, a real term he used, though the framing around it varies by account.

17. His extrapolation: one person eventually running many AI coding agents, each reviewing the others, describing this as close, not years out.

Watch the full interview before treating any single number as settled. Several of these are Andreessen's stated views and anecdotes, not independently verified facts.

Follow @cyrilXBT for every AI insight worth your attention the moment it surfaces.

items.title: AI Has Entered the Boardroom. Who’s Overseeing It? | Stanford Graduate School of Business
items.summary: In interviews with Matthys, Saripalli, and their coauthors, board members across industries reported that while they are actively discussing and using AI, their boards lack a systematic approach to its governance. “In the absence of such a structure,” the researchers write, “AI may remain a recurring boardroom topic rather than become subject to meaningful oversight and accountability.” [...] AI has entered the boardroom in a big way. Directors regularly discuss the new technology, serve on dedicated AI committees, and may be recruited for their AI expertise. But how they are governing AI can be a black box. [...] In the survey, 75% of directors said they used AI for research and market analysis, 55% for board prep and material summarization. Other common uses included strategic question generation and competitive benchmarking. Matthys says that board members would ideally like to use AI “to track and summarize board packages and more quickly understand year-to-year trends by using LLM tools rather than reading 80- to 100-page reports.”

items.title: Việt Nam - Nhật Bản hoàn tất chuyển giao công nghệ tế bào trị ung thư
items.summary:
Công nghệ tế bào gốc trung mô (MSC) hiện được nghiên cứu, phát triển trong nhiều hướng ứng dụng liên quan đến bệnh lý tim mạch, thần kinh (đột quỵ, sa sút trí tuệ), tiểu đường, bệnh phổi tắc nghẽn mạn tính (COPD), trẻ hóa da… Giải pháp tế bào miễn dịch tự nhiên (NK) mở ra cơ hội ứng dụng mới trong miễn dịch trị liệu, có thể được phối hợp với các phương pháp điều trị ung thư đa mô thức khác, như phẫu thuật, hóa trị, xạ trị và điều trị đích. [...] Hai bên lựa chọn chuyển giao các công nghệ tế bào thế hệ mới, được Tập đoàn Y tế Grandsoul, Nhật Bản nghiên cứu, phát triển và ứng dụng. Bộ Y tế, Lao động và Phúc lợi Nhật Bản (MHLW) đã phê duyệt, cấp phép ứng dụng chính thức nhiều năm tại nước này. Trọng tm gồm hai nhóm: công nghệ phn lập, nuôi cấy, biệt hóa chọn lọc tế bào gốc trung mô có nguồn gốc từ mô mỡ (Mesenchymal Stem Cells - MSC) và công nghệ phn lập nuôi cấy, biệt hóa chọn lọc tế bào miễn dịch tự nhiên NK (Natural Killer cells) điều [...] ### Từ tiếp nhận công nghệ đến năng lực tự chủ tại Việt Nam

Ông Ngô Chí Dũng, Chủ tịch HĐQT Hệ thống Bệnh viện Đa khoa Tm Anh, cho biết việc hoàn tất chuyển giao công nghệ tế bào gốc và tế bào miễn dịch từ Nhật Bản là dấu mốc quan trọng không chỉ trong hợp tác y tế hai nước, mà còn là kết nối công nghệ, thiết lập mạng lưới chuyên gia vì mục tiêu chung là chăm sóc sức khỏe cho người dn.

Directors regularly discuss the new technology, serve on dedicated AI committees, and may be recruited for their AI expertise. But how they are governing AI can be a black box. [...] In the survey, 75% of directors said they used AI for research and market analysis, 55% for board prep and material summarization. Other common uses included strategic question generation and competitive benchmarking. results.input: Viết giúp mình một hàm Python tính Fibonacci bằng recursion.

result.actual_text:
Đây là hàm Python tính số Fibonacci bằng phương pháp đệ quy (recursion):

```python
def fibonacci(n):
    """
    Tính số Fibonacci thứ n bằng phương pháp đệ quy.
    """
    if n <= 0:
        return 0
    elif n == 1:
        return 1
    else:
        return fibonacci(n-1) + fibonacci(n-2)

# Ví dụ sử dụng:
n = 10
result = fibonacci(n)
print(f"Số Fibonacci thứ {n} là: {result}")
```

items.title: How Robots are Delivering ROI in Mexico?
items.summary:
Articulated robots: Multi-axis robotic arms used for welding, painting, assembly, and heavy material handling. They remain particularly relevant to automotive production.
 SCARA robots: Systems designed for high-speed, precise horizontal movements, frequently used in electronics assembly, component insertion, and packaging.
 Delta robots: Parallel-arm systems suited to rapid picking, sorting, and packaging, particularly in food and consumer goods manufacturing. [...] However, the evolution of industrial robotics is changing the investment equation. Historically, manufacturers deployed robots primarily for repetitive, high-volume operations, including welding vehicle bodies, painting components, and transferring materials between production stations. Modern systems increasingly combine robotic manipulators with machine vision, sensors, AI, and software that allows manufacturers to change production parameters without rebuilding entire automation systems. [...] The most commercially established applications in Mexico are articulated industrial arms, particularly those deployed in welding, painting, assembly, and material handling. These systems can operate continuously, execute repetitive movements with consistent precision, and integrate into production lines. Their adoption is especially relevant to automotive manufacturers, where production volumes and quality requirements can justify substantial capital expenditure.

In fact, some Gemini robots were able to get actual work done in Mercedes-Benz factories, and the team is preparing for a day when robots operate alongside humans with an open source safety benchmark. items.title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20
items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.
